q-154066.name: Question 1
q-154066.problem: The length $l$ of a knife blade is $14\,\text{cm}$ to the nearest $1\,\text{cm}.$ Determine the upper and lower bounds of this measurement.
q-154066.worked_solution:
Our measurement is given to the nearest $1\,\text{cm}.$ So, the greatest possible error of this measurement is

$$
\frac{1\,\text{cm}}{2}=0.5\,\text{cm}.
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the lower and upper bounds of this measurement as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{lower bound} & =14\,\text{cm}-0.5\,\text{cm} \\  & =13.5\,\text{cm} \\ \text{upper bound} & =14\,\text{cm}+0.5\,\text{cm} \\  & =14.5\,\text{cm}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the exact value of $l$ lies between the lower and upper bound, we conclude that

$$
13.5\,\text{cm}\le l<14.5\,\text{cm}.
$$

q-154066.html:
Question 1
?

The length l of a knife blade is 14cm to the nearest 1cm. Determine the upper and lower bounds of this measurement.

a
13.9cm≤l<14.1cm
b
13cm≤l<15cm
c
13.95cm≤l<14.05cm
d
13.5cm≤l<14.5cm
e
4cm≤l<24cm
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Our measurement is given to the nearest 1cm. So, the greatest possible error of this measurement is

1cm2=0.5cm.

Therefore, we can calculate the lower and upper bounds of this measurement as follows:

lower bound=14cm−0.5cm=13.5cmupper bound=14cm+0.5cm=14.5cm

Since the exact value of l lies between the lower and upper bound, we conclude that

13.5cm≤l<14.5cm.

q-154064.name: Question 2
q-154064.problem: The distance $d$ between two lampposts is $40\,\text{m}$ to the nearest $10\,\text{m}.$ Determine the upper and lower bounds of this measurement.
q-154064.worked_solution:
Our measurement is given to the nearest $10\,\text{m}.$ So, the greatest possible error of this measurement is

$$
\frac{10\,\text{m}}{2}=5\,\text{m}.
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the lower and upper bounds of this measurement as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{lower bound} & =40\,\text{m}-5\,\text{m} \\  & =35\,\text{m} \\ \text{upper bound} & =40\,\text{m}+5\,\text{m} \\  & =45\,\text{m}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the exact value of $d$ lies between the lower and upper bound, we conclude that

$$
35\,\text{m}\le d<45\,\text{m}.
$$

q-154064.html:
Question 2
?

The distance d between two lampposts is 40m to the nearest 10m. Determine the upper and lower bounds of this measurement.

a
35.5m≤d<44.5m
b
39.5m≤d<40.5m
c
39m≤d<41m
d
30m≤d<50m
e
35m≤d<45m
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Our measurement is given to the nearest 10m. So, the greatest possible error of this measurement is

10m2=5m.

Therefore, we can calculate the lower and upper bounds of this measurement as follows:

lower bound=40m−5m=35mupper bound=40m+5m=45m

Since the exact value of d lies between the lower and upper bound, we conclude that

35m≤d<45m.

q-218706.name: Question 3
q-218706.problem:
The time $t$ it took Noah to run $200\,\text{m}$ was $31.2\,\text{s}$ to the nearest tenth of a second. Determine the upper and lower bounds of this measurement.

{{field-1}}$\text{s}$
$\,\le t<$
{{field-2}}$\text{s}$
q-218706.worked_solution:
Our measurement is given to the nearest $0.1\,\text{s}.$ So, the greatest possible error of this measurement is

$$
\frac{0.1\,\text{s}}{2}=0.05\,\text{s}.
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the lower and upper bounds of this measurement as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{lower bound} & =31.2\,\text{s}-0.05\,\text{s} \\  & =31.15\,\text{s} \\ \text{upper bound} & =31.2\,\text{s}+0.05\,\text{s} \\  & =31.25\,\text{s}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the exact value of $t$ lies between the lower and upper bound, we conclude that

$$
31.15\,\text{s}\le t<31.25\,\text{s}.
$$

\begin{aligned}\text{lower bound} & =2,693.1\,\text{mi}-0.05\,\text{mi} \\  & =2,693.05\,\text{mi} \\ \text{upper bound} & =2,693.1\,\text{mi}+0.05\,\text{mi} \\  & =2,693.15\,\text{mi}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the exact value of $d$ lies between the lower and upper bound, we conclude that

$$
2,693.05\,\text{mi}\le d<2,693.15\,\text{mi}.
$$

q-46382.name: Question 5
q-46382.problem: The dimensions of the cover of a chemistry book are $28\,\text{cm}\times 14\,\text{cm}$, where each dimension is measured to the nearest $1\,\text{cm}.$ Rounded to the nearest square centimeter, what is the smallest possible area of the book's cover?
q-46382.worked_solution:
Each dimension is given to the nearest $1\,\text{cm}.$ So, the greatest possible error of these measurements is

$$
\frac{1\,\text{cm}}{2}=0.5\,\text{cm}.
$$

We wish to find the *smallest* possible area of the book's cover. Therefore, we require the *lower bound* of each dimension.

The lower bounds for each dimension are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & 28\,\text{cm}-0.5\,\text{cm}=27.5\,\text{cm} \\  & 14\,\text{cm}-0.5\,\text{cm}=13.5\,\text{cm}\end{aligned}
$$

So,  the smallest possible area of the book's cover is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =27.5\,\text{cm}\times 13.5\,\text{cm} \\  & =371.25\,{\text{cm}}^{2} \\  & ≈371\,{\text{cm}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest square centimeter.

q-218721.name: Question 6
q-218721.problem:
The dimensions of a stamp are $2.1\,\text{cm}\times 2.4\,\text{cm}$, where each dimension is measured to the nearest $0.1\,\text{cm}.$ Rounded to the nearest tenth of a square centimeter, what is the upper bound for the area of the stamp?

To the nearest tenth of a square centimeter, the upper bound is
{{field-1}}${\text{cm}}^{2}.$
q-218721.worked_solution:
Each dimension is given to the nearest $0.1\,\text{cm}.$ So, the greatest possible error of these measurements is

$$
\frac{0.1\,\text{cm}}{2}=0.05\,\text{cm}.
$$

We wish to find the *upper bound* for the area of the stamp. Therefore, we require the *upper bound* of each dimension.

The upper bounds for each dimension are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & 2.1\,\text{cm}+0.05\,\text{cm}=2.15\,\text{cm} \\  & 2.4\,\text{cm}+0.05\,\text{cm}=2.45\,\text{cm}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the upper bound for the area of the stamp is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =2.15\,\text{cm}\times 2.45\,\text{cm} \\  & =5.267\,5\,{\text{cm}}^{2} \\  & ≈5.3\,{\text{cm}}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest tenth of a square centimeter.
